genre: Cricket trump-card duel / collectible card battler
title: T20 Super Over Trumps: Cricket Card Duels
audience: Cricket fans aged 13-35 (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, UK, Australia, South Africa, diaspora) who want a 2-minute competitive fix, enjoy stat arguments and bragging rights with friends, and like collecting complete sets of cricketer cards. Secondary: trump-card nostalgia players who grew up with playground stat card games.
controls: Touch only, one hand. TAP a stat row on the card to choose it, and tap again to confirm (or use a quick double-tap for speed mode). SWIPE UP on the card for Aggressive (flame trail and a red glow), and SWIPE DOWN for Safe (blue shield glow). TAP a power card in the tray to arm it, then pick the ball. LONG-PRESS any card to inspect the full stat sheet and the T20I/ODI/Test tabs. DRAG to arrange the deck in the Deck Builder. A pinch-free UI keeps everything one-handed, and every tap target is at least 48dp. Colour-blind-safe icons sit beside the colours. The emote wheel opens with a tap on the emote button (6 fixed emotes), and there is no text input anywhere.
core_loop: DUEL (about 2 min): both sides are dealt a hand from their deck of 12 cards, and the duel is one over of 6 balls. Each ball, the active batter's card is revealed face-up and the bowler's card is hidden. The active player taps one stat (e.g. strike rate, average, centuries, wickets, economy, catches). The higher value wins the ball, and the stat margin converts to runs (1, 2, 3, 4 or 6, from margin bands) for the winner. A tie sends the ball to a pot that is added to the next ball's winner. Before tapping, the player may swipe the card up to go AGGRESSIVE (runs x2 on a win, and a loss gives the opponent +2 extra runs and costs a "wicket") or swipe down to play SAFE (runs capped at 2, and a loss gives the opponent only 1). After 6 balls the higher run total wins. If the totals are tied, a 3-card sudden-death Super Over decides it. Power cards (Free Hit, Review, Powerplay) add one-use tactical swings. REWARD: coins, stars (1 to 3), a trophy bump, XP and pack progress. META: open earned packs, fill albums, upgrade cards with duplicate "form points", build a deck of 12, climb the ladder, do the daily chase, keep a streak, and duel friends. Then repeat.

positioning: The cricket trump-card game done to Marvel Snap and Clash Royale standards. Every duel is a 6-ball over that takes about 2 minutes. Cricket arguments ("who has the better average?") become a skill game: read the card, pick the stat, and decide whether to go aggressive or play safe. Real career numbers for T20I, ODI and Test make every card feel like a debate won or lost. Packs are earned, never bought as a gamble. A 60-rival ladder, a daily chase, albums and online duels give people a reason to open the game every day. Players are cartoon avatars with altered spellings, and the game uses no league, board or franchise marks.
progression: PLAYER META: (1) Trophy ladder and Player Level (XP) unlock modes and features. (2) COLLECTION: about 480 cartoon-avatar cards, grouped into Albums by country, role (openers, finishers, spinners, pacers, keepers, all-rounders) and era. Each album page completed gives a chest of coins plus a guaranteed named card. (3) CARD FORM: duplicates become Form Points that raise a card's "Form" tier (Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum) for small stat boosts of up to +5% in non-ranked ladder play; online duels use normalised stats to keep fair play, with cosmetic tier flair only. (4) DECK BUILDER: 12-card deck with a captain slot and 3 power-card slots, plus saved loadouts. (5) STREAKS: a daily login streak with a 7-day pack milestone, plus win streak multipliers on coins. (6) STAR GOALS: 180 stars across 60 rivals unlock chapter-star chests at 15, 30 and 45 stars per chapter. (7) DAILY CHASE: a handcrafted daily puzzle-like target (e.g. "Score 24 runs in 6 balls with a given 6-card hand, no wickets"). It is the same for all players, with a global country leaderboard. (8) WEEKLY FORMAT CUP with a leaderboard. (9) SEASON TRACK (30 days): free and premium cosmetic lanes, plus earned packs. (10) PACK SYSTEM: packs are earned only via wins, star chests, milestones and rewarded video. They use visible odds, and a deterministic pity timer guarantees a rare card every 5 packs and an epic card every 20. No paid random packs. Players may also spend coins or gems on a chosen specific card (direct-buy, rotating shop). (11) CHAPTER REWARDS: each chapter completion unlocks a new pitch theme, a card back, an emote and a story cutscene card (the cartoon commentator mascot). (12) STATS-AS-OF BANNER: every card shows a "stats as of <date>" line, and a live-ops stats refresh adds a "New Season Stats" event.

Stylised crowds with parallax and reactive cheers on boundaries.
No league, board or franchise colours, logos or marks.

level_structure:
CONTENT UNITS: 60 handcrafted rival duels across 6 themed chapters of 10 rivals each. Each rival is a named city-style team (generated name, no league or franchise marks) with a handcrafted deck, an AI personality, a fixed rule set and a signature "aha". Within each chapter, rivals 1-3 teach, 4-6 combine, 7 is a breather, 8 is a spike, 9 is a twist, and 10 is a boss duel with a Super Over finish. Every duel is a 6-ball over (about 2 min); boss duels are best-of-two overs. Stars: 1 star for a win, 2 stars for winning by 8+ runs, 3 stars for winning with no wickets lost (or in a perfect over, per the rival's goal). 

CHAPTER 1, GULLY GREENS (1-10): Core rules. Tap a stat, the higher value wins runs, ties go to the pot. Rival 5 introduces the Super Over, and the boss (10) forces a Super Over. Tone: friendly, wide margins, a tutorial overlay that fades.
CHAPTER 2, AGGRO ALLEY (11-20): Introduces AGGRESSIVE/SAFE swipes. 11-13 teach them one at a time. 14-16 give an opponent weak in the aggressive stat. 17 is a breather. 18 is a spike where the AI baits you. 19 uses a target chase (need 18 runs in 6 balls). 20 is a boss who always plays aggressive.
CHAPTER 3, POWER PAVILION (21-30): Introduces power cards one at a time: Free Hit (21-23: choose the stat after seeing the opponent card's top stat band), Review (24-26: undo a lost ball once), Powerplay (27-29: balls 1-2 count double). 30 is a boss duel with all three.
CHAPTER 4, FORMAT FORTRESS (31-40): Format packs. T20 weights strike rate and economy x1.5. ODI weights average and wickets. Test weights centuries and averages, and strike rate is nearly worthless. Rotating format rules per ball. Captain bonus is introduced (one card per deck gets +15% on one stat). 40 is a boss that switches format mid-over.
CHAPTER 5, TWIST TOWN (41-50): Fog of War (the opponent's card stays face-down until you pick a stat), Wildcard stat swap (swap one stat between your two cards once per over), and Pot Carry-over (ties stack across the over, with a mega pot of up to 4 balls). 50 is a boss using all three.
CHAPTER 6, GRAND SUPER SERIES (51-60): Combined mastery. Every mechanic returns with tougher AI. 51-54 are mixed-rule duels. 55 is a breather. 56-58 are hard-mode chases. 59 is the semi-final. 60 is the final, with a best-of-three overs finish and a Super Over.

After the ladder: Endless "Rival Rematch" (harder decks, bonus packs), a Daily Chase (see progression), Weekend Format Cups, and online Quick Duel plus Room Code modes.
difficulty_curve: Target win rate for an average new player: Ch1 85%, Ch2 70%, Ch3 65%, Ch4 55%, Ch5 50%, Ch6 40%. Each chapter follows this rhythm: teach (easy), combine (medium), breather at rival 7, spike at rival 8, twist at rival 9, boss at rival 10. Specific spikes: rival 18 (bait AI), 28 (Powerplay counter), 38 (format switch), 48 (fog + carry-over), 58 (hard-mode chase). Specific breathers: rival 7, 17, 27, 37, 47 and 55. Dynamic assist: after 3 consecutive losses the AI's deck quality drops slightly and the player receives a free Review. After 5 losses the game offers a rewarded-video "Coach hint" that highlights the best stat. The AI uses three personalities (Cautious, Balanced, Gambler) and a skill value that rises from 0.2 to 0.95 across the ladder. The AI is never given hidden information about the player's face-down cards, so there is no cheating. Each match is generated from a seeded handcrafted deck so replays are fair.
camera_orientation: Portrait, one-handed. Cards are held in the lower thumb zone, the opponent's card sits at the top, and the scoreboard strip runs across the middle. All actions are reachable with the thumb.
market_opportunity: Live Play data shows "Cricket Card Game" at roughly 50K installs and "Cricket Cards" at roughly 500, so the niche is thin while T20 cricket search volume is huge. The organic gate is weak: autocomplete for "cricket card battle" scores 0.27 and winnability is 0.59. We therefore anchor the store listing on high-volume phrases ("cricket", "T20", "trump cards", "cricket card game") and not on "card battle". Revenue comes from rewarded video, remove-ads, cosmetic card backs and pitch themes, a season pass of cosmetics and earned packs, and direct-buy (non-random) cards. Virality comes from room codes, shareable "my best XI" and album-completion images, and country leaderboards.
competitor_contrast: Existing cricket card apps are mostly static stat-compare toys with ugly UI, no depth and no progression. We add: (1) six-ball over scoring with a Super Over tiebreaker; (2) aggressive or safe risk-reward swipes; (3) power cards (Free Hit, Review, Powerplay); (4) format packs where T20, ODI and Test weight stats differently; (5) a 60-rival campaign with new rules every chapter; (6) earned packs and albums with visible odds and no paid randomness; (7) online quick duels and room codes with fixed emotes; (8) premium animated cartoon avatars and top-tier game feel.
economy_monetization:
CURRENCIES: Coins (soft: duel wins, chests, streaks), Gems (premium: season pass, milestones, IAP), Form Points (duplicate cards), and Pack Tokens (earned). SINKS: direct-buy cards (rotating shop), pack opening bonuses, cosmetic pitch themes and card backs, deck loadout slots, and rematch tickets. 

ADS (rewarded, always opt-in): +1 free pack per day (up to 3), double duel coins, free Review/Free Hit refill before a boss, a "Coach hint" after losing, and a revive-style "Extra Ball" in the Super Over. INTERSTITIALS: only after a completed duel, never during a duel, max one every 3 duels, and none in the first 15 minutes, in online matches, or for remove-ads buyers. 

IAP (light): Remove Ads (about $3.99, which also keeps rewarded video optional); Season Pass cosmetics ($4.99); cosmetic bundles (card backs, pitch themes, bat and boundary effects); gem and coin bundles (no random rewards); Starter Pack (a chosen set of 5 specific named cards plus coins, one time). No gambling, no loot boxes, and no paid random packs. All pack odds are shown in a visible table. Online duels use normalised stats, so IAP offers no pay-to-win advantage there. 

TARGET KPIs: D1 retention 45%, D7 18%, D30 7%. ARPDAU $0.10 to $0.18, ad-led, with 3 to 5% IAP conversion.
technical_assumptions: REVIEW FLAG: real-person likeness. All players use altered name spellings (reuse displayName from the Auction League data files) and cartoon avatars only, never photos. Store text never names real players. Legal review is recommended before release.
REVIEW FLAG: no league, tournament, board or franchise marks, names or colours. Team cards use country/city-style names only. Stats are international only (T20I, ODI, Test).

REVIEW FLAG: real stats are compiled from public scorecard records. They live in a single data file (e.g. data/cricketerStats.json) with an 'asOf' date, shown on cards as 'stats as of <date>'. Stats are never invented or rounded into fiction, and a refresh pipeline plus an automated validator checks the data (matches, runs, average, strike rate, 100s, 50s, HS, wickets, bowling average, economy, best bowling, catches).

Avatar assets are copied INTO the workspace from ~/Documents/other/Auction League/ipl-auction-game/assets/player-avatars (never editing that repo) and renamed to altered spellings. Missing players are recreated in the same 2D style.

React Native with Skia for cards, effects and the pitch, and Reanimated for gestures (swipe up/down) and animations. Target 60fps on mid-range Android (3GB RAM), with texture atlases and lazy-loaded avatars.

Game logic is a deterministic, seeded pure TypeScript engine (duel, scoring bands, pot, Super Over, power cards, format weights), unit-tested and shared between client and server for online validation.

Online: lightweight backend (e.g. Firebase or Supabase plus serverless functions) for matchmaking, room codes, server-authoritative duel resolution, leaderboards, and the daily chase seed. Anonymous auth, generated names, a fixed emote set and no chat. Every online mode falls back to an AI opponent after 8 seconds of waiting or on a disconnect.
Offline-first for the ladder, albums, daily chase (cached) and pass-and-play.
Normalised stats for online duels to keep fair play. Pack odds are visible with a deterministic pity timer, and no paid random rewards.
Ads through a mediation SDK, with consent (GDPR/UMP), child-directed settings off (13+ target), and local save with cloud backup.
Localisation-ready (English, Hindi, Urdu, Bengali and Sinhala later), with numerals and layouts that scale.
Size budget under 150MB through on-demand avatar packs.
qa_acceptance_criteria: A full 6-ball duel completes in under 3 minutes and resolves with a correct winner, including ties and the pot.
Tapping a stat compares the correct values, and the run conversion follows the documented margin bands for every format.
Swipe up (aggressive) doubles the win reward and applies the loss penalty. Swipe down (safe) caps at 2 runs. Gestures are distinguishable from taps and from scrolling.
Super Over triggers on tied totals, uses exactly 3 cards, and resolves sudden death with no further ties (a deterministic final tiebreaker).
Free Hit, Review and Powerplay each work once per duel, are blocked after use, and cannot be stacked illegally.
Format rules (T20/ODI/Test weights) and the captain bonus change outcomes exactly as specified, with unit tests for all format and stat combinations.
Fog of War, Wildcard swap and Pot Carry-over behave as specified in chapter 5 rivals.
All 60 ladder rivals load, are winnable, follow their chapter's mechanics, and award 1 to 3 stars with the right criteria. Progression gates unlock in order and save correctly.
Every card shows a 'stats as of' line, and every stat comes from the single stats data file. A validator test fails on missing or out-of-range values.
No real player's exact name appears anywhere in the app, and no league, board or franchise name, logo or colour appears. Store text names no real players.
Packs are earned only. Visible odds match the actual drop logic over 10,000 simulated opens, and the pity timer guarantees a rare card every 5 packs and an epic card every 20.
No paid random rewards, no gambling-like UI, no chat, and no typed text. Online emotes come only from the fixed set of 6.
Online quick duel matches within 8 seconds or falls back to an AI opponent. Room codes work for two players, and a disconnect hands the win/loss fairly or switches to AI.
Rewarded ads are always opt-in and grant the reward only on completion. Interstitials never appear during a duel, in the first 15 minutes, in online matches, or after Remove Ads.
Remove Ads and restore purchases work on both Android and iOS.
60fps on mid-range Android devices during card flips and effects, cold start under 4 seconds, and no crash across a 30-minute soak test.
Everything is playable one-handed in portrait, tap targets are at least 48dp, and a colour-blind mode, sound and haptics toggles, and reduced-motion option work.
Analytics events fire with correct parameters for all key flows (duel, ball, pack, ad, IAP, online).
Daily chase is the same for all players on a given day, resets at local midnight, and stores the score on the leaderboard.
